definitions.explanation: Having value or worth; deserving of attention, effort, or respect.

examples.japanese: {価値|かち}ある{体験|たいけん}だった。
{価値|かち}ある{情報|じょうほう}を{手|て}に{入|い}れた。
{時間|じかん}をかけてでも{読|よ}む{価値|かち}ある{本|ほん}を{紹介|しょうかい}したい。
examples.english: I want to recommend books that are worth reading even if they take time.

notes:
A pre-noun modifier combining {価値|かち} (value, worth) and ある (to exist). It functions as an attributive expression placed directly before a noun, meaning "having value" or "worthwhile."

This pattern (noun + ある) is a classical Japanese construction that survives in modern written and somewhat formal spoken Japanese. Other examples include {意味|いみ}ある (meaningful) and {力|ちから}ある (powerful).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {価値|かち}ある{体験|たいけん}: a valuable experience
- {価値|かち}ある{情報|じょうほう}: valuable information
- {価値|かち}ある{存在|そんざい}: a worthy existence
- {読|よ}む{価値|かち}がある: worth reading

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {貴重|きちょう}な: precious, valuable — emphasizes rarity and preciousness
- {有意義|ゆういぎ}な: meaningful, significant — emphasizes purposefulness
- {価値|かち}がある: to have value — the predicative form (used at the end of a sentence rather than before a noun)
